data.gender_notes: Giselle is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word gisellein, meaning 'to pledge' or 'to give as a hostage'. In the Middle Ages, it was a common name for noblewomen who were given to enemy princes to ensure peace. The name was later popularized by the Romantic ballet Giselle. The name Giselle carries the meaning “Pledge, Hostage, Beautiful Stranger” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Giselle usually hope their child will grow to embody pledge, hostage, beautiful stranger and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes faith and commitment, as a pledge or hostage given in trust.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Giselle total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

Giselle is a tale of love, betrayal, and redemption set against the backdrop of a woodland community and the supernatural world of the Wilis. The ballet has become a classic, inspiring numerous adaptations and interpretations, shaping the landscape of the dance world.
